chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Whoever falls ill for a night and accepts it with its (proper) acceptance, God Almighty and Majestic shall record for him the worship of sixty years.'
I said: 'What is the meaning of its acceptance?' He said: 'He does not complain of what has afflicted him during it to anyone.'

key_terms.عبادة: Worship/devotion — the acts of obedience and submission offered to God
key_terms.قبول: Acceptance/reception — here meaning patient, silent acceptance of illness without complaint
key_terms.يشكو: To complain/lament — the act of expressing grievance about one's suffering to others

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for accepting illness with patience in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that a single night of illness, when accepted with true patience — meaning without complaining to others — is rewarded by God with the equivalent of sixty years of worship. When asked to define this 'acceptance,' the Imam clarified it as refraining from complaint to any person. This hadith connects Shia ethical teaching on sabr (patience) with the transformative spiritual merit of bearing suffering silently and with full contentment.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who gets sick for a night and he accepts it with an acceptance, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Write for him worship performed for sixty years’.
I said, ‘What is the meaning of ‘an acceptance’?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He does not complain of what has afflicted him during it, to anyone’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kindiy from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that if one becomes ill in a night and accepts it in the way it has come, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, on the other hand, writes down for him the reward for sixty years of worship.
I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is the meaning of “accepts it?”’
The Imam said, ‘He does not complain before any of his visitors against his illness.’”
